## Summary

I implemented the duplicate-telephone rejection on owner creation.

**Change** — `src/main/java/.../rest/controller/v1/OwnerRestControllerV1.java`, in `addOwner`:

After the existing normalization step (strip non-digits, require exactly 10 digits), I added a check that compares the new owner's normalized telephone against the normalized telephone of every existing owner. On a match it returns **409 Conflict**; otherwise creation proceeds as before.

```java
owner.setTelephone(telephone);
boolean telephoneInUse = this.clinicService.findAllOwners().stream()
    .map(Owner::getTelephone)
    .filter(Objects::nonNull)
    .map(existing -> existing.replaceAll("\\D", ""))
    .anyMatch(telephone::equals);
if (telephoneInUse) {
    return new ResponseEntity<>(HttpStatus.CONFLICT);
}
this.clinicService.saveOwner(owner);
```

**Design notes:**
- The check lives right beside the existing telephone normalization/`BAD_REQUEST` logic in the controller, matching the established style (this codebase signals status by returning `ResponseEntity` directly rather than throwing; there was no existing 409 path or duplicate exception to reuse).
- Both sides of the comparison are normalized the same way (`replaceAll("\\D","")`), so it enforces the rule on the *normalized* value regardless of how a stored telephone was originally formatted — exactly what the spec asks.
- Placed after the `BAD_REQUEST` guard, so invalid input still returns 400 and only well-formed-but-duplicate numbers return 409.

**Tests:** `coreRejectsDuplicateTelephone` (expects 409) and `functionalityAllowsDistinctTelephone` (expects 2xx) both pass; full suite is green.
